blindSummary:
This state/province's court of appeals annulled the entire trial over the killing of a transgender woman, holding that the country's "femicide" (femicidio) offence - the strongest gendered-violence protection in the penal code - covers only "a person biologically female" and therefore the conviction could not stand as framed. The case: a 55-year-old trans woman whose body was found on the southern coast of this state/province's capital in June 2022; her killer had been convicted at first instance to presidio perpetuo, and on the defence's nullity motion the appeals court declared the whole trial void in early October 2023. A named judicial finding that, in this jurisdiction, the most severe legal protection available for gender-motivated violence does not extend to trans women. This state/province accounted for 1.56 % of the national anti-LGBTI case total in 2024 - a small-share region where a single structural finding dominates the record.

The legal framework is unchanged (the gender-identity law and the femicide article both remain in force nationally), but the regional judiciary's operative interpretation in this instance creates a concrete protection gap for a trans person assaulted in this state/province.
